raw_response: The figure presents a horizontal bar chart comparing the percentage of GDP expenditure above a reference value of 2021 across several European countries. The vertical axis displays country names, listed in descending order based on the value represented by the bars. The horizontal axis, labeled "% über dem Referenzwert von 2021," ranges from 0 to 4, with tick marks at 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4. Error bars are present at the end of each bar. The bars are divided into two colored sections, representing "Anstieg zwischen 2021 und 2024" (shown in blue) and "Ausgaben 2021" (shown in green). The bar for Polen has a length of approximately 3.5, with the blue section representing roughly 1.5 and the green section roughly 2. The bar for Estland has a length of approximately 3.2, with the blue section representing roughly 1.2 and the green section roughly 2. The bar for Lettland has a length of approximately 3.1, with the blue section representing roughly 1.1 and the green section roughly 2. The bar for Litauen has a length of approximately 2.9, with the blue section representing roughly 0.9 and the green section roughly 2. The remaining bars generally decrease in length, with the shortest bar for Spanien having a length of approximately 0.5, with the blue section representing roughly 0.2 and the green section roughly 0.3. A legend at the bottom identifies the colors representing the two expenditure categories.
